content: <thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the base peak at m/z 183.045 is taken as the molecular ion (M⁺). The isotopic pattern shows a strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base), characteristic of a single chlorine atom (⁷⁵Cl/⁷⁷Cl ≈ 3:1). Subtracting the mass of one ³⁵Cl (34.968 Da) leaves a mass of ≈148.076 Da to be composed of C, H, and O. A composition of C₉H₈O₂ (exact monoisotopic mass = 148.052 Da) together with one Cl gives a calculated molecular ion mass of 183.021 Da, which matches the observed m/z 183.045 within typical experimental error. Therefore the most plausible molecular formula is C₉H₈O₂Cl.
